newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: India-Pakistan peace talks set for March 28-31.
newsitem.headline: India-Pakistan peace talks set for March 28-31.

text.p: Pakistan said on Thursday it would resume stalled peace talks with arch-rival India at a senior official level in New Delhi on March 28.
A Foreign Ministry statement said the talks between foreign ministry secretaries Shamshad Ahmad of Pakistan and Salman Haider of India would last until March 31.

"Pursuant to the exchange of letters between the prime ministers of Pakistan and India, it has been decided that the foreign secretaries of the two countries will meet in New Delhi on March 28-31," the brief Pakistani announcement said.
The last round of talks between the South Asian neighbours was held in January 1994 but they bogged down due to differences over the Himalayan region of Kashmir.

India and Pakistan have fought three wars, two of them over Kashmir, since they gained independence from Britain in 1947. New Delhi accuses Islamabad of arming and training separatist guerrillas fighting Indian rule in Jammu and Kashmir state. Pakistan says it provides only moral and diplomatic support.
Following Nawaz Sharif's election as Pakistan's prime minister last month, India and Pakistan have exchanged letters expressing a desire to resume bilateral talks.
